text:
sara: Heads up — observed a latency regression on A100 for long sequences (>2048). Kernel picker started picking `generic-slab` instead of the `warp-specialized` path after yesterday's autotune change. p95 spiked ~30%. Anyone seen this? :thinking_face:

aditya: Which commit/autotune change? Can you paste the perf numbers and model/seq details?

mike: Quick numbers from our microbench (gpt-small-ish, batch=1):
```
Before (master@2026-03-10): p50=18ms p95=46ms
After (autotune/regen-tiles): p50=20ms p95=60ms
Seqlen=2300
```
Looks like p95 mostly affected.

anya: Two quick suspects: register pressure forcing generic path, or the LUT thresholds for seqlen->kernel mapping got nudged. Also if KV prefetch is on for long sequences we might be burning shared mem.

sara: Reproducer attached: infra-bot linked profiling flame and nvprof summary.

infra-bot: Artifact: https://ci.internal/redwood/artifacts/1999000123/profiles/ (flamegraph + nvprof txt)

aditya: Checked autotune diff: the LUT entry for A100 in the new table reduced tile_slab for seq ranges >1536 (it used to stay at 64 until 2048). Looks like a conservative move to avoid reg-spill on some quantized kernels. That change makes picker prefer `generic-slab` for 1536-4096.

mike: If the change was meant to avoid register spills on quantized int8 kernels, could we make the LUT arch-aware (a100 vs h100) and also seqlen-aware? For A100 the warp-specialized 64 tile still fits regs for fp16.

anya: Agreed. Quick patch idea:
```
# kernel_picker.cfg
[chooser]
arch_overrides = { "a100": { "seqlen_threshold": 2048, "tile_slab": 64 }, "h100": { ... }}
```
Also toggle KV prefetch for long sequences:
kv_prefetch.long_seq_threshold = 2048
kv_prefetch.enabled = true
kv_prefetch.bypass_for_long_seq = true
```
That bypass reduces SMEM usage during generation when hits are sparse.

sara: I ran a quick A/B: forcing tile_slab=64 for A100 brings p95 back to ~48ms. KV prefetch bypass gave additional ~6% win on p95 for sequences that have low cache hit ratio.

aditya: Two actions:
1) Revert the conservative LUT change for A100 and add an arch-aware override (small PR).
2) Add a canary/regression test that runs microbench at seqlen=2300 and measures p95 delta < 10%.
I'll open the PR and the test. PR in my queue: #4129

mike: I'll run a small sweep with tile_slab in {48,64,80} across batch={1,4} and kv_prefetch on/off on a100 lanes 2/3. Posting results when done.

anya: Also let's add a debug probe in the picker to log why it chose generic vs warp-specialized (tile/regs/smem reason). Short term we'll get visibility without re-profiling every change.

infra-bot: Scheduled microbench run: https://ci.internal/redwood/runs/1999000140 — results will be attached.

sara: Thanks. Once PR is up can we do a staged rollout? Start with Dedicated A100 fleets, then host. We should avoid affecting H100 configs.

aditya: Yep. Canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% rollout. I'll include arch gating in the rollout job.

mike: Preliminary sweep results (short): tile=48 p95=52ms, tile=64 p95=47ms, tile=80 p95=49ms. Prefetch off improved tail for seqlen with poor KV hit by ~5%.

sara: Perfect — that matches local. Thanks all. I'll track PR #4129 and the canary. :thumbsup:

anya: I'll add the picker debug logs and a note in the autotune docs about arch-aware thresholds.

mike: LMK if you want me to run the same on h100 to verify we don't regress there.

sara: Yes please run h100 too but keep the default conservative LUT for h100 until we verify. Closing the loop once CI runs finish.

infra-bot: Test run finished: https://ci.internal/redwood/runs/1999000180/results — artifacts: flamegraphs, kernel-chooser logs

sara: Marking this as tracked. Follow-ups: PR #4129, picker-logs PR, canary schedule. Thanks everyone.
